comparison: Both evaluate the rescue experiments (C105-C111, C114-C116). OpenEval finds the evidence strongly supports causality with appropriate controls and anatomical specificity. Peer reviewers also support these findings, noting they address concerns about specificity, though cell-type specificity concerns remained.

Both address quinine control experiments (C47-C48, C90-C91, C130). OpenEval finds these effectively rule out taste sensitivity as the primary driver of nicotine aversion. Peer reviewers agree, with Reviewer #1's concerns about bitterness sensitivity appearing to be satisfied by these control experiments.

Both evaluate ternary plot analysis of behavioral strategies (C49-C53, C56-C57). OpenEval finds the methodology rigorous and well-controlled. Peer Reviewer #1 expresses uncertainty, questioning whether the plot is sufficient for dissecting populations and noting apparent heterogeneity between avoiders and non-avoiders.

Both address baseline consumption parameters (C35-C39, C117). OpenEval finds these provide essential confirmatory context. Peer reviewers accept these basic characterizations without specific concerns, though the overall model was criticized for translational relevance.

Both evaluate ex vivo patch-clamp data linking IPN responses to behavior (C28, C62-C65). OpenEval finds the mechanistic link well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with concerns about insufficient addressing of β4-nAChR differences between avoiders/non-avoiders and potential sampling variability rather than chronic nicotine effects.

Both address the discrepancy with prior literature regarding nAChR regulation (C147-C154). OpenEval finds the authors' reconciliation scientifically sound based on cell-type specificity and experimental timing. Peer Reviewer #3 notes this finding contradicts multiple studies across labs and species, requesting improved discussion of this key discrepancy.

Both evaluate behavioral evidence from two-bottle choice experiments (C27, C40-C45). OpenEval finds converging evidence with clear classification criteria and adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with concerns about the sufficiency of the pseudo-ternary plot, sample size determination, and limited translational relevance of the oral drinking model.

Both address temporal persistence of aversion (C58-C61, C138). OpenEval finds the dose-switching experiments demonstrate learning/conditioning mechanisms. Peer reviewers support these findings (R12) without specific concerns. However, R12 also includes C140-C142 about the two-stage model, which OpenEval addresses separately in R18.

Both evaluate Chrnb4-/- knockout experiments (C84-C89, C94-C95, C103-C104). OpenEval finds strong genetic evidence with robust phenotype and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting clarification on β4 distribution in IPN, cell-type specificity, and documentation of in vivo IPN activity changes in knockout mice.

Partial overlap on chronic nicotine behavioral effects (C76-C79, C83). OpenEval (R3) finds complementary evidence from multiple methodologies supporting adaptation and tolerance. Peer reviewers (R4) support the behavioral findings showing reduced avoidance after chronic nicotine, though the underlying mechanism was questioned elsewhere.

Both address chronic nicotine treatment effects (C66-C68, C75, C146). OpenEval finds the causal chain from reduced IPN responses to increased consumption well-established. Peer Reviewer #3 identifies the downregulation finding as contradictory to multiple studies showing upregulation, noting it 'remains at odds with other findings in the literature.'

Both address in vivo IPN response characterization (C69-C71, C64, C100). OpenEval finds the anatomical correlation and activity-response relationships well-controlled and internally consistent. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the heterogeneity of IPN neurons and request better documentation of recording locations and cell-type specificity.

Both address the two-stage aversion model (C140-C142). OpenEval finds the distinction between IPN-dependent initiation and broader circuit-dependent maintenance conceptually important, though C142 is noted as speculative. Peer reviewers support the persistence findings without specific concerns about this interpretation.

Minimal overlap (C81). OpenEval (R11) evaluates individual-level analysis of chronic nicotine effects with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers (R4) accept the behavioral findings from chronic treatment without specific concerns about the individual-level analysis.

Minimal overlap (C85). OpenEval (R12) evaluates anatomical characterization using genetic reporter. Peer reviewers (R5) request clarification on β4 distribution in IPN and cell-type specificity, suggesting this anatomical information was insufficient.
